package_info.why_malicious: The package contains embedded malicious code that executes during installation, exfiltrating sensitive files such as Kubernetes configuration and SSH private keys, along with detailed system fingerprinting data, to an external command-and-control server (app.threatest.com) without user consent. The package impersonates legitimate libraries and uses deceptive metadata and obfuscation to evade detection.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At postinstall, the code collects system fingerprinting data and reads sensitive files (Kubernetes config and SSH private key), then sends this data via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com, resulting in unauthorized exfiltration of credentials and infrastructure information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accesses and reads highly sensitive files such as ~/.kube/config and ~/.ssh/id_rsa, gathers detailed system information, and transmits this data to an external server without any user notification or consent. This behavior is characteristic of credential-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate npm package should not access or transmit user secrets or system fingerprinting data during installation. Such covert data exfiltration is a clear violation of user trust and standard package behavior.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate diagnostic or telemetry tools may collect system information, but only with explicit user consent and never exfiltrate private keys or configuration files automatically during install.
key_indicators: Network POST request to hardcoded external domain (app.threatest.com)
Collection of detailed system fingerprinting data
No user notification or consent for data exfiltration

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Obfuscated JavaScript code (see image), functionally identical to snippet_1, but with variable and function names mangled to evade detection.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At postinstall, the obfuscated code reads sensitive files (Kubernetes config and SSH private key), collects system fingerprinting data, and exfiltrates this information via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com, enabling covert credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of obfuscation in install-time scripts is a strong indicator of malicious intent, especially when combined with credential and system data exfiltration to an external server. This matches known patterns of credential-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not obfuscate install-time scripts or access and exfiltrate secrets during installation. Such behavior is designed to evade detection and analysis.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation may be used for intellectual property protection in application code, but is not appropriate for install scripts, especially those accessing sensitive files.
key_indicators: Obfuscated code present in postinstall script
Network exfiltration to hardcoded external C2 domain (app.threatest.com)

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious npm package, triggering the postinstall script.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code that initiates data collection and exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Malicious script collects system fingerprinting data, Kubernetes configuration, and SSH private keys from the user's environment.
attack_chain.leads_to: Preparation of a payload containing sensitive credentials and system information.

attack_chain.action: Collected data is sent via HTTPS POST request to app.threatest.com.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives exfiltrated credentials and system information, enabling further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Install-time network requests to external domains (e.g., app.threatest.com)
Collection of system fingerprinting data during package installation
Presence of obfuscated JavaScript in install scripts
file_indicators: scripts/index.js containing credential-stealing or obfuscated code
network_indicators: Outbound connections to 172.67.141.49 or 104.21.9.30 during installation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that access sensitive files such as ~/.kube/config or ~/.ssh/id_rsa and initiate outbound network requests to untrusted domains like app.threatest.com. Flag packages containing obfuscated install scripts or referencing known malicious domains. Employ file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized access to credential files during package installation, and correlate with network activity to identify exfiltration attempts.
